neighbours.label: a process noun that predicts 'products' next (combustion / decay / breakdown / fission products)
fire: Gas heaters must vent their combustion products through a flue.
Ammonia is one of the breakdown products of amino acids.
Radon and its decay products build up in basements.
Spent fuel contains many fission products of uranium.
Smoke contains the oxidation products of burning wood.
Lactate is a waste product of muscle metabolism during sprints.
Carbon dioxide is a byproduct of fermentation by yeast.
The degradation products of the plastic leach into soil.
quiet: Gas heaters must be serviced by a licensed engineer every year.
Ammonia has a sharp smell that fills the whole room.
Radon gas is colourless and has no smell at all.
Spent fuel is stored underwater for several years.
Smoke drifted over the valley for most of the afternoon.
Muscles grow stronger after weeks of regular sprints.
Yeast is added to the dough before it is left to rise.
The plastic bags were buried in the soil behind the shed.

notes: logit effect: the + pole suppresses 'products'; probes on combustion / breakdown read 0.74-0.88.
